assets.title: Moscow & Kremlin Skyline
assets.details: High aerial view over the Moskva River, capturing the historic red-brick towers of the Moscow Kremlin, Cathedral of Christ the Saviour, and golden cathedral domes.

assets.title: Crimean Mountain Peaks
assets.details: Spectacular flight over the limestone precipices and karst plateaus of the Crimean Mountains rising dramatically above the azure waters of the Black Sea.

assets.title: Siberian Taiga & Inya River
assets.details: The Siberian taiga represents the largest continuous forest biome on Earth, dominated by larch, spruce, and Siberian pine. Gliding above the winding Inya River, the dense untouched canopy stretches uninterrupted across thousands of kilometers of northern wilderness.

assets.title: Lake Baikal Winter Turquoise Ice
assets.details: Lake Baikal is the world's oldest and deepest freshwater lake, containing over 20% of the world's unfrozen surface fresh water. In winter, the crystalline Siberian waters freeze into translucent turquoise ice sheets, towering hummocks, and intricate geometric fissures across an endless frozen horizon.

assets.title: Golden Mountains of Altai
assets.details: A UNESCO World Heritage site situated at the junction of Russia, Kazakhstan, Mongolia, and China. The Altai Mountains showcase dramatic alpine ridges, glaciated cirques, and dense Siberian larch taiga valleys preserving one of Earth's most pristine high-altitude ecosystems.

assets.title: Kamchatka Volcanic Wilderness
assets.details: The Kamchatka Peninsula in the Russian Far East is one of the most volcanically active regions on the Pacific Ring of Fire. Colossal stratovolcanoes rise majestically above wild boreal forests, geothermal river valleys, and pristine arctic wilderness.

assets.title: Rila Monastery
assets.details: Founded in the 10th century by Saint John of Rila, this Eastern Orthodox monastery sits at 1,147 m in the forested Rila Mountains. Renowned for its distinctive striped colonnades, intricate vibrant frescoes, and the 14th-century stone Tower of Hrelyo, it stands as Bulgaria's cultural and spiritual sanctuary.

assets.title: Seven Rila Lakes
assets.details: A group of glacial lakes situated in the northwestern Rila Mountains between 2,100 and 2,500 meters altitude. Cascading into each other from the highest 'The Tear' to 'The Eye', 'The Kidney', 'The Twin', 'The Trefoil', 'Fish Lake', and 'The Lower Lake', they form Bulgaria's most visited alpine wonderland.

assets.title: Belogradchik Rocks and Fortress
assets.details: A striking formation of reddish and yellowish sandstone and conglomerate rock pinnacles sculpted over 200 million years, reaching up to 200 meters high on the western slopes of the Balkan Mountains. Built naturally into the towers is the ancient Belogradchik Fortress, dating back to Roman times.

assets.title: Ancient City of Nessebar
assets.details: An ancient Black Sea peninsula with over 3,000 years of civilization, known as the 'Pearl of the Black Sea'. Connected to the mainland by a narrow isthmus with a wooden windmill, this UNESCO World Heritage town showcases remarkable medieval churches, timber houses, and seaside fortifications.

assets.title: Alexander Nevsky Cathedral, Sofia
assets.details: One of the largest Eastern Orthodox cathedrals in the world, built in Neo-Byzantine style with gold-plated and copper domes soaring 53 meters high. Serving as the primary cathedral of the Bulgarian Patriarchate, it dominates the historic heart of Sofia.

assets.title: Buzludzha Monument
assets.details: Perched atop Mount Buzludzha at 1,441 m along the Central Balkan Mountains ridge, this colossal saucer-shaped brutalist structure and 70-meter tower was opened in 1981. Now an enigmatic world-renowned relic of 20th-century history, it stands amid sweeping panoramic mountain vistas.

assets.title: Old Town & Roman Theatre, Plovdiv
assets.details: Continuously inhabited for over 8,000 years, Plovdiv is one of the oldest cities in Europe. Its historic Old Town spreads across three granite hills (Nebet Tepe), featuring ornate National Revival mansions and a remarkably preserved 1st-century Roman amphitheatre overlooking the city.

photos.title: Christ the Redeemer — Paul Landowski, 1931, Corcovado, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil
photos.description: Colossal Art Deco statue of Jesus Christ created by French sculptor Paul Landowski and Brazilian engineer Heitor da Silva Costa. Standing 30 meters tall atop the 700-meter Corcovado peak overlooking Rio de Janeiro, it was constructed between 1922 and 1931 from reinforced concrete and six million soapstone tiles. In 2007, it was voted one of the New Seven Wonders of the World.

photos.title: David — Michelangelo, 1504, Galleria dell'Accademia, Florence, Italy
photos.description: Masterpiece of Renaissance sculpture created in pure Carrara marble by Michelangelo between 1501 and 1504. Standing 5.17 meters tall, the statue portrays the biblical hero David, poised with intense focus before facing Goliath. Its anatomical accuracy and contrapposto stance established it as the supreme symbol of Florentine civic liberty.

photos.title: Mask of Tutankhamun — 18th Dynasty Gold Mask, c. 1323 BC, Luxor / Cairo, Egypt
photos.description: Ancient Egyptian gold funerary mask of the 18th Dynasty pharaoh Tutankhamun, crafted around 1323 BC. Discovered in 1925 in the Valley of the Kings by Howard Carter, it is fashioned from two sheets of beaten high-karat gold inlaid with colored glass, faience, and semi-precious lapis lazuli.

photos.title: Great Sphinx of Giza — Old Kingdom Colossal Sculpture, c. 2500 BC, Giza, Egypt
photos.description: Colossal limestone statue of a reclining mythical sphinx with the body of a lion and the head of Pharaoh Khafre, carved around 2500 BC during Egypt's Old Kingdom. Measuring 73 meters long and 20 meters high, it is the oldest known monumental sculpture in Egypt.

photos.title: Benin Bronzes — Kingdom of Benin Royal Sculptures, 16th c., Benin City, Nigeria
photos.description: Group of over a thousand commemorative brass and bronze plaques and cast sculptures created by the Edo people of the Kingdom of Benin from the 16th century onward. Adorning the royal palace of the Oba, their intricate lost-wax casting exemplifies West African metalworking mastery.

photos.title: Church of St. George — Rock-Hewn Monolithic Church, c. 1200, Lalibela, Ethiopia
photos.description: Monolithic cross-shaped church carved directly downward into volcanic tuff rock during the late 12th or early 13th century under King Gebre Mesqel Lalibela. Connected by a subterranean network of trenches and catacombs, it remains an active pilgrimage site of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church.

photos.title: Great Mosque of Djenné — Sudano-Sahelian Earth Architecture, c. 13th c., Djenné, Mali
photos.description: The largest mud-brick architecture in the world, situated along the Bani River in Mali. Built in the distinctive Sudano-Sahelian architectural style with sun-baked earth bricks, its walls are replastered annually by the entire community during an extraordinary cultural festival.

photos.title: Ife Head of a King — Kingdom of Ife Brass Sculpture, c. 1300, Ife, Nigeria
photos.description: Masterpiece of Yoruba naturalistic sculpture cast in copper alloy around 1300 AD in the ancient sacred city of Ile-Ife. Unearthed in 1938, its refined facial features and delicate striations represent an Ooni (king) wearing a beaded royal headdress.

photos.title: The Great Wave off Kanagawa — Hokusai, c. 1831, Mount Fuji, Japan
photos.description: Famous woodblock print by the Japanese ukiyo-e master Katsushika Hokusai, published around 1831 as the first print in Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji. Depicts towering rogue waves framing Japan's sacred Mount Fuji, with three oared cargo boats bravely navigating the turbulent seas.

photos.title: Along the River During the Qingming Festival — Zhang Zeduan, Song Dynasty, Bianjing, China
photos.description: Panoramic Song Dynasty handscroll painting by Zhang Zeduan from the early 12th century, capturing the vibrant daily life, commerce, and celebrations in the imperial capital of Bianjing (modern Kaifeng) along the Yellow River during the annual Qingming festival.

photos.title: Terracotta Army — Qin Dynasty Sculptures, c. 210 BC, Xi'an, China
photos.description: Monumental funerary collection of more than 8,000 life-sized terracotta soldiers, 130 chariots, and 520 horses buried around 210 BC to protect Qin Shi Huang, the first Emperor of China, in the afterlife. Every single soldier displays unique facial features, armor, and hairstyles.

photos.title: Taj Mahal — Mughal Monumental Architecture, 1648, Agra, India
photos.description: Ivory-white marble mausoleum on the south bank of the Yamuna River, commissioned in 1631 by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan to house the tomb of his favorite wife, Mumtaz Mahal. Celebrated as the jewel of Muslim art in India, it features symmetry, Persian calligraphy, and pietra dura inlays.

photos.title: Ajanta Rock-Cut Cave Temples — Vakataka Dynasty, c. 475 AD, Maharashtra, India
photos.description: Monumental rock-cut Buddhist cave sanctuaries carved into a horseshoe-shaped basalt cliff gorge in the Sahyadri hills of Maharashtra, India, under the Vakataka Dynasty around 475 AD. Comprising 30 prayer halls (chaityas) and monasteries (viharas), it is a UNESCO World Heritage masterpiece.

photos.title: Kandariya Mahadeva Temple — Chandela Dynasty, c. 1030 AD, Khajuraho, India
photos.description: The largest and most ornate Hindu temple at Khajuraho, built around 1030 AD by the Chandela king Vidyadhara. Dedicated to Lord Shiva, its towering spire represents Mount Meru, adorned with over 800 intricately carved sculptures celebrating divine joy and artistic perfection.

photos.title: Angkor Wat — Khmer Monumental Architecture, c. 1150 AD, Siem Reap, Cambodia
photos.description: Massive temple complex constructed in the early 12th century by Khmer King Suryavarman II, originally dedicated to Vishnu before transforming into a Buddhist center. Spanning over 160 hectares, it is the largest religious monument in the world, surrounded by a vast moat.

photos.title: Borobudur Temple Stupas — Sailendra Dynasty, c. 800 AD, Java, Indonesia
photos.description: The world's largest Buddhist temple, built in the 8th and 9th centuries under the Sailendra Dynasty. Constructed without mortar from volcanic rock, its concentric terraces ascend past 2,672 relief panels and 504 Buddha statues toward a central monumental dome.

photos.title: Gate of All Nations — Achaemenid Empire, c. 515 BC, Persepolis, Iran
photos.description: Grand entrance portal ordered by King Xerxes I around 515 BC at Persepolis, the ceremonial capital of the Persian Achaemenid Empire. Guarded by colossal winged human-headed bulls (lamassu), it welcomed envoys and dignitaries from all provinces of the vast empire.

photos.title: El Castillo (Pyramid of Kukulkan) — Maya Civilization, c. 900 AD, Chichen Itza, Mexico
photos.description: Mesoamerican step-pyramid dedicated to the feathered serpent deity Kukulkan, built by the Maya civilization between the 9th and 12th centuries. During the equinoxes, the afternoon sun casts shadows creating the illusion of a giant serpent slithering down the stairs.

photos.title: Pyramid of the Sun — Pre-Columbian City, c. 200 AD, Teotihuacan, Mexico
photos.description: The largest structure in the ancient pre-Columbian city of Teotihuacan, built around 200 AD along the Avenue of the Dead. Rising 65 meters above the valley floor, it served as an astronomical observatory and ceremonial temple dedicated to celestial deities.

photos.title: Aztec Sun Stone (Piedra del Sol) — Aztec Empire, c. 1502, Tenochtitlan / Mexico City
photos.description: Colossal basalt calendar monolith carved in the early 16th century by the Mexica (Aztec) Empire under Emperor Moctezuma II. Unearthed beneath Mexico City's Zócalo in 1790, it depicts the central face of the sun god Tonatiuh surrounded by four previous cosmic eras.

photos.title: Machu Picchu Sanctuary — Inca Empire, c. 1450, Andes Mountains, Cusco, Peru
photos.description: Inca royal citadel situated on a mountain ridge 2,430 meters above sea level in the Sacred Valley of Peru, constructed around 1450 under Emperor Pachacuti. Known for its sophisticated dry-stone masonry, agricultural terraces, and dramatic alpine panorama.

photos.title: Moai of Rapa Nui — Polynesian Monolithic Statues, c. 1250–1500, Easter Island, Chile
photos.description: Monolithic volcanic stone figures carved by the Polynesian Rapa Nui people between 1250 and 1500 AD. Representing ancestral chiefs, nearly 1,000 statues stand across the remote Pacific island, gazing inland from monumental stone platforms called ahu.

photos.title: American Gothic — Grant Wood, 1930, Eldon, Iowa / Art Institute of Chicago
photos.description: Iconic 1930 regionalist painting by Grant Wood, inspired by the Carpenter Gothic house in Eldon, Iowa. Depicting a farmer holding a pitchfork alongside his daughter, it captures the stoic spirit and work ethic of small-town rural America during the Great Depression.

photos.title: Nighthawks — Edward Hopper, 1942, New York / Art Institute of Chicago
photos.description: Atmospheric 1942 oil painting by Edward Hopper portraying four late-night patrons seated in an illuminated downtown diner on a quiet city corner. Renowned for its subtle depiction of urban solitude, cinematic lighting, and modernist architectural geometry.

photos.title: Aboriginal Rock Art — Indigenous Australian Ancestral Art, Kakadu, Australia
photos.description: Ancient Indigenous Australian rock art gallery in Kakadu National Park, Northern Territory, dating back over 20,000 years. Painted by Bininj/Mungguy artists using natural ochre pigments, it documents ancestral creation stories, native wildlife, and the spiritual Rainbow Serpent.

photos.title: Mona Lisa — Leonardo da Vinci, c. 1503, Musée du Louvre, Paris, France
photos.description: Celebrated Renaissance portrait painted in oil on poplar wood by Leonardo da Vinci, begun around 1503 in Florence. Famous for its subtle sfumato blending, enigmatic smile, and imaginary mountainous landscape, it is the most visited painting in the Musée du Louvre.

photos.title: The Starry Night — Vincent van Gogh, 1889, Saint-Rémy-de-Provence, France
photos.description: Post-impressionist masterpiece painted by Vincent van Gogh in June 1889 from his asylum room window at Saint-Rémy-de-Provence. Features swirling celestial rhythms, glowing crescents and stars, and an expressive foreground cypress tree.

photos.title: The Birth of Venus — Sandro Botticelli, c. 1485, Uffizi Gallery, Florence, Italy
photos.description: Renaissance canvas painted around 1485 by Sandro Botticelli, depicting the goddess Venus emerging from the sea upon a scallop shell, blown ashore by the winds Zephyr and Aura. Preserved in Florence's Uffizi Gallery, it embodies Neoplatonic humanist ideals.

photos.title: The Creation of Adam — Michelangelo, 1512, Sistine Chapel, Vatican City
photos.description: Monumental fresco painted by Michelangelo between 1508 and 1512 upon the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel. Illustrating the biblical creation narrative from Genesis, the nearly touching fingertips of God and Adam form one of the most celebrated gestures in Western art.

photos.title: The Thinker — Auguste Rodin, 1904, Musée Rodin, Paris, France
photos.description: Iconic bronze sculpture created by French sculptor Auguste Rodin, conceived in 1880 as part of The Gates of Hell inspired by Dante's Inferno. Depicts a muscular male figure leaning forward in deep philosophical meditation, symbolizing human contemplation and creative struggle.

photos.title: The Kiss — Gustav Klimt, 1908, Belvedere Palace, Vienna, Austria
photos.description: Sensual Golden Phase painting by Austrian symbolist Gustav Klimt, completed in 1908. Using gold leaf, silver, and intricate geometric patterns, it portrays two lovers wrapped in an ornate embrace atop a bed of wild alpine blossoms in Vienna's Belvedere Palace.

photos.title: Girl with a Pearl Earring — Johannes Vermeer, 1665, Mauritshuis, The Hague
photos.description: Exquisite Dutch Golden Age tronie painted around 1665 by Johannes Vermeer. Renowned for its luminous rendering of light, exotic blue turban, and reflective teardrop pearl, it captivates viewers with her momentary over-the-shoulder glance.

photos.title: The Night Watch — Rembrandt, 1642, Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam, Netherlands
photos.description: Monumental 1642 masterpiece by Rembrandt van Rijn, depicting Captain Frans Banninck Cocq and his civic militia company preparing to march. Acclaimed for its dramatic chiaroscuro lighting, dynamic motion, and life-size group composition in the Rijksmuseum.

photos.title: Venus de Milo — Alexandros of Antioch, c. 150 BC, Milos, Greece
photos.description: Classical Hellenistic marble sculpture carved around 150 BC on the Aegean island of Milos, attributed to Alexandros of Antioch. Standing over 2 meters tall, the graceful goddess of love and beauty is renowned worldwide for her classic S-curve contrapposto.

photos.title: Winged Victory of Samothrace — Hellenistic Sculpture, c. 190 BC, Samothrace, Greece
photos.description: Monumental Parian marble sculpture of the goddess Nike, created around 190 BC on the Greek island of Samothrace to celebrate a naval triumph. Perched upon a ship's prow with rippling drapery swept by sea winds, it presides over the Daru staircase in the Louvre.

photos.title: The Colosseum — Flavian Amphitheatre, 80 AD, Rome, Italy
photos.description: The largest ancient amphitheatre ever built, constructed in limestone, tuff, and brick-faced concrete under the Flavian emperors between 72 and 80 AD. Seating over 50,000 spectators for gladiatorial contests, it remains the ultimate architectural icon of Imperial Rome.

photos.title: The Parthenon & Acropolis — Classical Greek Architecture, c. 447 BC, Athens, Greece
photos.description: Former temple dedicated to the goddess Athena, constructed between 447 and 432 BC atop the rocky Acropolis of Athens by architects Ictinus and Callicrates under Pericles. Regarded as the zenith of Doric classical architecture and Western democratic heritage.

photos.title: The Scream — Edvard Munch, 1893, National Museum, Oslo, Norway
photos.description: Pioneering expressionist composition created in 1893 by Norwegian artist Edvard Munch. Depicting an agonized figure under an infernal orange sunset along the Kristiania fjord, it externalizes Munch's sensation of an infinite, piercing scream passing through nature.

photos.title: Las Meninas — Diego Velázquez, 1656, Museo del Prado, Madrid, Spain
photos.description: Complex Golden Age painting created in 1656 by Diego Velázquez in the Royal Alcázar of Madrid. Depicting the young Infanta Margaret Theresa attended by her retinue, with Velázquez himself at the easel and the King and Queen reflected in a rear mirror.

photos.title: Wanderer above the Sea of Fog — Caspar David Friedrich, 1818, Dresden / Hamburg
photos.description: Romantic oil painting by Caspar David Friedrich, completed in 1818. Depicting a lone traveler standing upon a rocky precipice gazing out over a sweeping landscape cloaked in mountain fog, it epitomizes the Romantic encounter with the sublime in nature.

photos.title: Madara Rider — Early Medieval Rock Relief, c. 710 AD, Madara, Bulgaria
photos.description: Early medieval monumental rock relief carved around 710 AD into a vertical 100-meter cliff near Madara in northeastern Bulgaria. Depicting a horseman triumphant over a lion, followed by a hunting dog, it is a UNESCO World Heritage site honoring the early Bulgarian rulers.

photos.title: Boyana Church Frescoes — Medieval Master, 1259, Boyana, Sofia, Bulgaria
photos.description: Medieval Bulgarian Orthodox church located at the foot of Mount Vitosha in Sofia. Its exceptional 1259 frescoes by a master Bulgarian iconographer display remarkable psychological depth, realism, and vibrant color, foreshadowing the European Renaissance by decades.

photos.title: Rila Monastery Frescoes — Zahari Zograf, c. 1844, Rila, Bulgaria
photos.description: The spiritual and cultural heart of Bulgaria, founded in the 10th century in the Rila Mountains. Its 1844 exterior frescoes by Zahari Zograf feature brilliant biblical scenes, angels, and virtues, representing the pinnacle of the Bulgarian National Revival.

photos.title: The Bronze Horseman — Étienne Falconet, 1782, Senate Square, Saint Petersburg, Russia
photos.description: Monumental equestrian statue of Peter the Great, commissioned by Catherine the Great and sculpted by Étienne Maurice Falconet between 1768 and 1782 on the bank of the Neva River. Peter points westward atop the Thunder Stone, the largest stone ever moved by humans.

photos.title: Morning in a Pine Forest — Ivan Shishkin, 1889, Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow, Russia
photos.description: Beloved 1889 Russian landscape painting by Ivan Shishkin, featuring four brown bear cubs playing among fallen trees in a misty primordial forest. Renowned for Shishkin's masterly depiction of morning sunlight filtering through ancient pine crowns.

photos.title: The Ninth Wave — Ivan Aivazovsky, 1850, State Russian Museum, Saint Petersburg, Russia
photos.description: Epic 1850 marine masterpiece by Russian romantic painter Ivan Aivazovsky. Depicting castaways clinging to a broken mast after a nocturnal storm as the luminous morning sun breaks through crashing ocean swells, it symbolizes hope amidst the raw power of the sea.

photos.title: Barge Haulers on the Volga — Ilya Repin, 1873, State Russian Museum, Saint Petersburg, Russia
photos.description: Seminal 1873 realist oil painting by Ilya Repin, depicting eleven exhausted burlaks (barge haulers) straining against heavy leather straps to pull a barge up the Volga River under the blazing sun. Praised by Tolstoy, it is an enduring tribute to human dignity.

photos.title: Fine Wind, Clear Morning (Red Fuji) — Hokusai, c. 1831, Edo / Mount Fuji, Japan
photos.description: Iconic woodblock print from Katsushika Hokusai's 'Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji' series. Depicts Mount Fuji bathed in reddish morning sunlight in late summer, with delicate white mackerel clouds drifting across an intense Prussian blue sky.

photos.title: Sudden Shower over Shin-Ōhashi Bridge — Utagawa Hiroshige, 1857, Edo / Tokyo, Japan
photos.description: Masterpiece woodblock print by Utagawa Hiroshige from 'One Hundred Famous Views of Edo' (1857). Shows pedestrians scrambling across the Great Bridge over the Sumida River during a violent summer cloudburst, famously admired and copied in oil by Vincent van Gogh.

photos.title: Plum Park in Kameido — Utagawa Hiroshige, 1857, Edo / Tokyo, Japan
photos.description: Celebrated woodblock print by Utagawa Hiroshige (1857) featuring the famous 'Sleeping Dragon Plum' tree (Garyūbai). The composition uses a bold, close-up foreground framing device that deeply influenced Western Post-Impressionism.

photos.title: Red and White Plum Blossoms — Ogata Kōrin, c. 1716, MOA Museum of Art, Atami, Japan
photos.description: National Treasure pair of two-panel folding screens by Ogata Kōrin (c. 1716), master of the Rinpa school. Features swirling metallic silver river waters flanked by stylized blooming plum trees, blending abstract graphic design with profound naturalism.

photos.title: Irises Screen — Ogata Kōrin, c. 1701, Nezu Museum, Tokyo, Japan
photos.description: National Treasure pair of six-panel folding screens by Ogata Kōrin (c. 1701), painted with precious azurite and malachite pigments on gold leaf. Illustrates an episode from the 10th-century 'Tales of Ise' at the Eight Bridges of Mikawa province.

photos.title: Cypress Trees Screen — Kanō Eitoku, 1590, Tokyo National Museum, Japan
photos.description: National Treasure eight-panel folding screen by Azuchi-Momoyama master Kanō Eitoku (1590). Executed in color and gold leaf on paper, it portrays a colossal, gnarled ancient cypress tree symbolizing enduring power and majesty.

photos.title: Otani Oniji III as Edobei — Tōshūsai Sharaku, 1794, Tokyo, Japan
photos.description: Famous Edo-period kabuki portrait print by the enigmatic master Tōshūsai Sharaku (1794). Depicts actor Otani Oniji III as the villainous servant Yakko Edobei with tensed hands, wild eyes, and open mouth, capturing an intense dramatic climax.

photos.title: Three Beauties of the Present Day — Kitagawa Utamaro, c. 1793, Edo / Tokyo, Japan
photos.description: Masterpiece ukiyo-e print by Kitagawa Utamaro (c. 1793) depicting three celebrated beauties of 1790s Edo: geisha Tomimoto Toyohina, and teahouse waitresses Naniwa Kita and Takashima Hisa, set against a sparkling mica-dusted background.

photos.title: Pine Trees in the Snow — Maruyama Ōkyo, 1780s, Mitsui Memorial Museum, Tokyo, Japan
photos.description: Pair of six-panel folding screens by Maruyama Ōkyo (1780s), designated a National Treasure of Japan. Executed in ink and light color with gold dust, it captures heavy snow resting on evergreen pine boughs using reserve white paper technique.

photos.title: Landscape in Splashed Ink (Haboku Sansui) — Sesshū Tōyō, 1495, Tokyo National Museum, Japan
photos.description: National Treasure hanging scroll by Zen Buddhist monk and master Sesshū Tōyō (1495). Created using the spontaneous 'splashed ink' (haboku) technique, expressing towering misty mountains and a solitary boatman with rapid, calligraphic brushstrokes.

photos.title: Travelers Among Mountains and Streams — Fan Kuan, c. 1000, National Palace Museum, Taipei
photos.description: Monumental Northern Song hanging scroll by Fan Kuan (c. 1000), widely regarded as the pinnacle of Chinese landscape painting. Towering granite cliffs rise above mist-shrouded valleys where a tiny pack mule caravan winds along a rocky path.

photos.title: Early Spring — Guo Xi, 1072, Northern Song Dynasty, National Palace Museum, Taipei
photos.description: National Treasure Northern Song hanging scroll by Guo Xi (1072). Demonstrates the 'three distances' perspective, capturing the awakening of nature after winter with vaporous mists, surging mountain ridges, and gnarled pine trees.

photos.title: On a Mountain Path in Spring — Ma Yuan, c. 1200, Southern Song Dynasty, National Palace Museum
photos.description: Exquisite Southern Song album leaf by Ma Yuan (c. 1200), known as 'One-Corner Ma' for his evocative asymmetric compositions. A scholar accompanied by a servant walks along a willow path while watching a singing oriole.

photos.title: Emperor Qianlong in Ceremonial Armor — Giuseppe Castiglione (Lang Shining), 1739, Beijing, China
photos.description: Monumental hanging scroll by Jesuit court painter Giuseppe Castiglione (Lang Shining, 1739). Depicts the Qing Dynasty Qianlong Emperor on horseback in full ceremonial gold armor, synthesizing European oil realism with Chinese ink tradition.

photos.title: Court Ladies of Former Shu — Tang Yin, c. 1520, Palace Museum, Beijing, China
photos.description: Renowned Ming Dynasty hanging scroll by Tang Yin (Tang Bohu, c. 1520), one of the Four Masters of Ming. Portrays four elegant imperial palace ladies in opulent Five Dynasties attire, painted with refined gongbi brushwork.

photos.title: Poet on a Mountaintop — Shen Zhou, c. 1490, Ming Dynasty, Nelson-Atkins Museum
photos.description: Celebrated Ming Dynasty album leaf by Shen Zhou (c. 1490), founder of the Wu School of literati painting. A solitary poet stands atop a windswept plateau gazing across rolling mist, accompanied by a self-inscribed poem on the harmony of mind and landscape.

photos.title: Autumn Colors on the Qiao and Hua Mountains — Zhao Mengfu, 1295, Yuan Dynasty
photos.description: Handscroll by Yuan Dynasty master Zhao Mengfu (1295), painted for his friend Zhou Mi. Depicts the distinctive rounded Mount Hua and cone-shaped Mount Qiao in Shandong province, ushering in the scholar-amateur literati style.

photos.title: Immortal in Splashed Ink — Liang Kai, c. 1200, National Palace Museum, Taipei
photos.description: Masterpiece album leaf by Southern Song painter Liang Kai (c. 1200). Rendered with miraculous economy of wet, abbreviated brushwork, capturing the eccentric, laughing spirit of a Chan Buddhist immortal in a few swift strokes.

photos.title: Dwelling in the Fuchun Mountains — Huang Gongwang, 1350, Yuan Dynasty
photos.description: Legendary Yuan Dynasty handscroll by Huang Gongwang (1350), one of the Four Masters of the Yuan. Painted over three years along the scenic Fuchun River in Zhejiang, revered as a supreme masterpiece of Chinese literati landscape art.

photos.title: Shakuntala Looking Back for Dushyanta — Raja Ravi Varma, 1898, Kerala / Bangalore, India
photos.description: Celebrated 1898 oil painting by Raja Ravi Varma depicting heroine Shakuntala from the Mahabharata pretending to remove a thorn from her foot while turning back to catch a secret glimpse of King Dushyanta in the forest.

photos.title: Damayanti Talking to the Swan — Raja Ravi Varma, c. 1899, Trivandrum, India
photos.description: Masterpiece oil painting by Raja Ravi Varma (c. 1899) illustrating the tale of Nala and Damayanti from the Mahabharata. Princess Damayanti listens intently as a celestial golden swan sings the praises of King Nala.

photos.title: Radha of Kishangarh (Bani Thani) — Nihâl Chand, c. 1750, National Museum, New Delhi, India
photos.description: Iconic 18th-century Rajput miniature by court painter Nihâl Chand (c. 1750), often called the 'Mona Lisa of India'. Depicts the singer and poet Bani Thani as the Hindu goddess Radha, with exaggerated lotus eyes, arched eyebrows, and sheer gold-bordered veil.

photos.title: Jahangir Preferring a Sufi Shaikh to Kings — Bichitr, c. 1620, Mughal Empire, Agra, India
photos.description: Intricate Mughal miniature from the St. Petersburg Album by court artist Bichitr (c. 1620). Depicts Emperor Jahangir seated on an hourglass throne presenting a book to a venerable Sufi mystic while European King James I and Ottoman Sultan look on.

photos.title: Krishna and Radha in a Pavilion — Pahari / Kangra School, c. 1780, Himachal Pradesh, India
photos.description: Exquisite Pahari miniature from the Kangra School (c. 1780) illustrating Jayadeva's Gita Govinda. The divine lovers Krishna and Radha embrace in an ornate marble pavilion under a dark monsoon sky illuminated by a streak of golden lightning.

photos.title: Galaxy of Musicians — Raja Ravi Varma, 1889, Mysore Palace, Karnataka, India
photos.description: Monumental 1889 oil canvas by Raja Ravi Varma painted for the Maharaja of Mysore. Depicts eleven Indian women in diverse regional traditional attire playing indigenous musical instruments, celebrating the unified cultural tapestry of India.

photos.title: Bride's Toilet — Amrita Sher-Gil, 1937, National Gallery of Modern Art, New Delhi, India
photos.description: Seminal 1937 modern oil painting by pioneer Indian modernist Amrita Sher-Gil. Depicts a young Indian bride dressed in luminous saffron surrounded by her family members, blending European post-impressionism with classical Ajanta cave fresco aesthetics.

photos.title: Shiva Nataraja (Lord of the Dance) — Chola Dynasty Bronze, 11th c., Thanjavur, Tamil Nadu, India
photos.description: 11th-century lost-wax bronze masterpiece of the Chola Dynasty from Tamil Nadu. Depicts the cosmic dance (Ananda Tandava) of Shiva within an aureole of flames, embodying the continuous cycle of creation, preservation, and destruction of the universe.

photos.title: The Court of Gayumars — Sultan Muhammad, c. 1522, Shahnameh of Shah Tahmasp, Tabriz, Iran
photos.description: Supreme masterpiece of Persian miniature painting from the Shahnameh of Shah Tahmasp, painted by Sultan Muhammad (c. 1522). Depicts King Gayumars enthroned atop a miraculous flowering mountain among court nobles clad in leopard skins.

photos.title: The Seduction of Yusuf (Joseph fleeing Zulaikha) — Kamāl ud-Dīn Behzād, 1488, Herat / Cairo
photos.description: Famous Persian miniature by Kamāl ud-Dīn Behzād (1488) illustrating Jami's Haft Awrang. Portrays Yusuf fleeing through seven locked rooms of an intricate labyrinthine palace designed by Zulaikha, celebrated for its brilliant architectural perspective.

photos.title: Two Lovers — Reza Abbasi, 1630, Safavid Empire, Isfahan, Iran
photos.description: Exquisite Safavid miniature painting by court master Reza Abbasi (1630) in Isfahan. Depicts two youthful lovers in an intimate embrace wrapped in rich Persian textiles, capturing the sensual elegance of 17th-century Isfahani courtly culture.

photos.title: Surname-i Vehbi Imperial Festival — Abdülcelil Levni, c. 1720, Topkapi Palace, Istanbul, Turkey
photos.description: Ottoman miniature by court painter Abdülcelil Levni (c. 1720) illustrating the imperial circumcision festival of Sultan Ahmed III. Depicts guild artisans and acrobats parading across the Hippodrome in Constantinople with lavish floats.

photos.title: Striding Lion Glazed Relief — Processional Way of Babylon, c. 575 BC, Mesopotamia / Iraq
photos.description: Neo-Babylonian glazed polychrome brick relief from the Processional Way of Babylon (c. 575 BC) during the reign of Nebuchadnezzar II. The sacred lion of the goddess Ishtar strided along the sacred ceremonial avenue to the Ishtar Gate.

photos.title: The Royal Lion Hunt of Ashurbanipal — Neo-Assyrian Relief, c. 645 BC, Nineveh / Mosul, Iraq
photos.description: Triumphant alabaster bas-relief from the North Palace of Nineveh (c. 645 BC). Depicts the great Assyrian king Ashurbanipal in his chariot hunting desert lions, celebrated worldwide for the intense muscular realism and pathos of the wounded animals.

photos.title: Achaemenid Immortals Glazed Frieze — Palace of Darius, c. 510 BC, Susa, Iran
photos.description: Glazed siliceous brick frieze from the Apadana Palace of Darius the Great at Susa (c. 510 BC). Depicts the elite elite Persian royal guard known as 'The Immortals', adorned in embroidered robes and armed with spears, bows, and quivers.

photos.title: Complete View of Mount Geumgang (Geumgangjeondo) — Jeong Seon, 1734, Joseon Dynasty, Korea
photos.description: National Treasure of Korea painted by Joseon master Jeong Seon (1734). Pioneered the True-View Landscape (Jingyeong Sansuwha) movement, capturing the sacred 12,000 serrated granite peaks of the Diamond Mountains with dynamic rhythmic brushwork.

photos.title: Ssireum (Korean Wrestling) — Kim Hong-do (Danwon), c. 1780, Joseon Dynasty, Seoul, Korea
photos.description: Iconic Joseon genre painting by Kim Hong-do (Danwon, c. 1780) from the Danwon Pungsokdo Album. Captures two wrestlers locked in a tense throw surrounded by a circular audience of animated spectators reacting with suspense and humor.

photos.title: Man, Controller of the Universe — Diego Rivera, 1934, Palacio de Bellas Artes, Mexico City
photos.description: Monumental 1934 fresco painted by Mexican muralist Diego Rivera at the Palacio de Bellas Artes in Mexico City, recreating his destroyed Rockefeller Center mural 'Man at the Crossroads'. Depicts humanity at the pivot of science, nature, industry, and social movements.

photos.title: The Valley of Mexico from the Hill of Santa Isabel — José María Velasco, 1877, Mexico
photos.description: Monumental 1877 landscape canvas by Mexican master José María Velasco. Captures the sweeping geological expanse of the Valley of Mexico with the Popocatépetl and Iztaccíhuatl volcanoes rising beneath majestic cumulus clouds.

photos.title: Murals of Bonampak (Musicians and Procession) — Maya Civilization, c. 790 AD, Chiapas, Mexico
photos.description: Ancient Maya fresco in Structure 1 of the ruins of Bonampak in Chiapas, Mexico (c. 790 AD). Shows Mayan royal musicians playing turtle carapaces, rattles, and long wooden trumpets in a vibrant ceremony painted with brilliant Maya Blue.

photos.title: The Raven and the First Men — Bill Reid, 1980, Haida Nation / Vancouver, Canada
photos.description: Monumental yellow cedar carving by master Haida artist Bill Reid (1980) at the Museum of Anthropology in Vancouver. Illustrates the Haida creation myth of Raven coaxing the first human beings out of a giant clamshell on the shores of Haida Gwaii.

photos.title: Moche Portrait Vessel of a Ruler — Moche Culture, c. 450 AD, Larco Museum, Lima, Peru
photos.description: Finely modeled stirrup-spout ceramic vessel of the Moche culture of ancient Peru (c. 450 AD). Features an individualized realistic human portrait of an elite Moche dignitary with ornate headdress, ear spools, and painted facial markings.

photos.title: Queen Nefertari Playing Senet — Tomb of Nefertari, c. 1255 BC, Valley of the Queens, Luxor, Egypt
photos.description: Vibrant 19th Dynasty Egyptian wall painting from the Tomb of Queen Nefertari (QV66) in the Valley of the Queens (c. 1255 BC). The Great Royal Wife of Ramesses II plays the game of senet to pass safely into the afterlife, wearing a pleated linen gown and vulture headdress.

photos.title: Nebamun Hunting in the Marshes — Tomb of Nebamun, c. 1350 BC, Thebes / Luxor, Egypt
photos.description: Famous 18th Dynasty Egyptian fresco fragment from the tomb-chapel of scribe Nebamun at Thebes (c. 1350 BC). Nebamun stands on a reed skiff in the papyrus marsh hunting birds with a throwstick, surrounded by lotus flowers and a hunting cat.

photos.title: Saint George and the Dragon — Ethiopian Diptych Icon, 17th c., Tigray, Ethiopia
photos.description: 17th-century Ethiopian Christian diptych icon from the Tigray highlands, painted in tempera on wood. Depicts Saint George mounted on a white charger slaying the dragon, executed in the distinctive vibrant, graphic Gondarine style.

photos.title: Olowe of Ise Carved Veranda Post — Yoruba Kingdom, c. 1910, Ekiti / Ikere, Nigeria
photos.description: Magnificent architectural veranda post carved from a single trunk of wood by master Yoruba sculptor Olowe of Ise (c. 1910) for the royal palace of Ikere. Depicts an equestrian warrior king atop a horse with extraordinary vertical dynamism.

photos.title: Earth's Creation — Emily Kame Kngwarreye, 1994, Utopia, Northern Territory, Australia
photos.description: Monumental 1994 masterpiece by senior Aboriginal Australian artist Emily Kame Kngwarreye. Executed in swirling dots and sweeps of synthetic polymer paint, depicting Alhalkere after the monsoonal rains in the Australian Central Desert.

photos.title: Carved Canoe Prow (Tauihu) — Māori Whakairo Wood Carving, 18th c., Aotearoa / New Zealand
photos.description: 18th-century Māori war canoe prow (tauihu) carved from native tōtara wood with pounamu jade chisels. Features intricate spirals (pitau) and stylized ancestral guardian figures (manaia) with iridescent pāua shell eyes, personifying ocean navigation power.

photos.title: Portrait of a Beauty (Miindo) — Shin Yun-bok (Hyewon), c. 1805, Joseon Dynasty, Seoul, Korea
photos.description: Masterpiece genre painting by Joseon Dynasty master Shin Yun-bok (Hyewon, c. 1805). Portrays an elegant gisaeng with an elaborate braided hairstyle (eonjeun meori) touching the norigae ornament of her hanbok, revered as the epitome of Korean feminine beauty.

photos.title: Wang Xizhi Watching Geese — Qian Xuan, c. 1295, Yuan Dynasty, Metropolitan Museum of Art
photos.description: Yuan Dynasty handscroll by Qian Xuan (c. 1295), one of the Eight Talents of Wuxing. Depicts the legendary 4th-century Calligrapher Sage Wang Xizhi leaning from a pavilion watching swimming geese, whose fluid neck movements inspired cursive calligraphy.

photos.title: Yashoda and Krishna — Raja Ravi Varma, c. 1890s
photos.description: Beloved late-19th-century oil painting by Indian master Raja Ravi Varma depicting the foster-mother Yashoda tenderly holding the infant Lord Krishna, blending European academic realism with classical Hindu iconography.

photos.title: Head Study — Rabindranath Tagore, c. 1930
photos.description: Expressive modernist ink and wash portrait of a human face by Nobel laureate and painter Rabindranath Tagore (c. 1930), housed in the Indian Museum, Kolkata. Tagore turned to visual art in his sixties, creating haunting, psychological character studies.

photos.title: Woman — Rabindranath Tagore, c. 1930
photos.description: Luminous modernist painting of a woman by Rabindranath Tagore (c. 1930), characterized by rhythmic, veiled contours and melancholic chiaroscuro that helped pioneer Indian modernism.

photos.title: Landscape — Rabindranath Tagore, c. 1930
photos.description: Atmospheric twilight landscape painted by Rabindranath Tagore in the 1930s, silhouetting dark Bengal trees against a glowing amber horizon with brooding poetic intensity.

photos.title: Young Girls — Amrita Sher Gil, 1932
photos.description: Breakthrough 1932 oil on canvas by Hungarian-Indian modernist Amrita Sher-Gil, depicting her sister Indira alongside friend Denise Proutaux in Paris. The painting won the Gold Medal at the 1933 Grand Salon in Paris, making Sher-Gil the youngest Associate of the Salon.

photos.title: Three Girls — Amrita Sher Gil, 1935
photos.description: Landmark 1935 painting ('Group of Three Girls') painted by Amrita Sher-Gil shortly after returning to India from Paris. Portrays three young Punjabi women in quiet, introspective silence using flat, glowing planes of crimson, ochre, and emerald.

photos.title: Between the Spider and the Lamp — M. F. Husain, 1956
photos.description: Iconic modernist canvas 'Between the Spider and the Lamp' (1956) by Indian master Maqbool Fida Husain, blending folk sensibilities, bold calligraphic lines, and symbolic figuration.

photos.title: Horse with a Bouquet — M. F. Husain, c. 1960s
photos.description: Dynamic modernist painting 'Horse with a Bouquet' by M. F. Husain, showcasing his signature galloping equine motif rendered in energetic, cubist-inflected planes of color.

photos.title: Yellowface — M. F. Husain, c. 1960s
photos.description: Vibrant expressionist canvas 'Yellowface' by Progressive Artists' Group co-founder M. F. Husain, combining mythic Indian narrative forms with bold modern chromatic contrasts.

photos.title: Kanchenjunga — Nicholas Roerich, c. 1930s
photos.description: Radiant tempera mountain landscape by Russian master Nicholas Roerich (1936), depicting the sacred five-peaked massif of Kanchenjunga in the Himalayas bathed in crystalline cobalt, violet, and rose alpenglow.

photos.title: Madonna Oriflamma — Nicholas Roerich, 1932
photos.description: Symbolic 1932 tempera painting by Nicholas Roerich portraying a Renaissance-inspired Madonna holding unfurled the Banner of Peace—three red spheres within a circle representing Art, Science, and Religion.

photos.title: Himalayas — Nicholas Roerich, various years
photos.description: Luminous Himalayan mountain vista painted in Sikkim by Nicholas Roerich, known as the 'Master of the Mountains' for his jewel-like tempera depictions of high-altitude peaks and spiritual solitude.

photos.title: Mahishasura — Tyeb Mehta, 1996
photos.description: Celebrated 1997 acrylic on canvas by Indian modernist Tyeb Mehta, reinterpreting the ancient mythic struggle between the goddess Durga and the buffalo demon Mahishasura through razor-sharp diagonal planes of crimson, ochre, and black.

photos.title: Composition VII — Wassily Kandinsky, 1913
photos.description: Composition VII is a 1913 abstract oil painting by Russian-born painter Wassily Kandinsky. It is in the collection of the Tretyakov Gallery, in Moscow. Art historians have concluded that the work is a combination of the themes of Resurrection, Judgment Day, the Flood and the Garden of Eden.

photos.title: Composition VIII — Wassily Kandinsky, 1923
photos.description: Masterpiece of geometric abstraction painted by Wassily Kandinsky in July 1923 while teaching at the Bauhaus in Weimar, now in the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum. Features a symphony of circles, triangles, grids, and intersecting lines.

photos.title: Yellow Red Blue — Wassily Kandinsky, 1925
photos.description: Monumental 1925 Bauhaus oil painting ('Gelb-Rot-Blau') by Wassily Kandinsky at the Musée National d'Art Moderne, Centre Pompidou, contrasting a radiant warm yellow geometric left side against a cool mystical blue circle on the right.

photos.title: Ivan the Terrible and His Son Ivan — Ilya Repin, 1885
photos.description: Ivan the Terrible and His Son Ivan on 16 November 1581 is a painting by Russian realist artist Ilya Repin made between 1883 and 1885. It depicts the grief-stricken Russian tsar Ivan the Terrible cradling his dying son, the Tsarevich Ivan Ivanovich, shortly after Ivan the Terrible had dealt a fatal blow to his son's head in a fit of anger.

photos.title: Reply of the Zaporozhian Cossacks — Ilya Repin, 1891
photos.description: Reply of the Zaporozhian Cossacks is a painting by Ukrainian-born Russian realist artist Ilya Repin. It is also known as Cossacks of Saporog Are Drafting a Manifesto and Cossacks are Writing a Letter to the Turkish Sultan.

photos.title: Rye — Ivan Shishkin, 1878
photos.description: Rye (Russian: Рожь), sometimes A Rye Field, is an oil painting finished in 1878 by the Russian painter Ivan Shishkin. It depicts a field of rye near the village of Lekarevo, west of Yelabuga in Tatarstan.

photos.title: In the Wild North — Ivan Shishkin, 1891
photos.description: Poetic 1891 winter nocturnal landscape by Russian realist Ivan Shishkin, inspired by Mikhail Lermontov's poem. Depicts a solitary snow-laden pine standing atop a sheer cliff under cold moonlight.

photos.title: The Persistence of Memory — Salvador Dalí, 1931
photos.description: Surrealist icon painted in 1931 by Salvador Dalí, housed in the Museum of Modern Art (MoMA), New York. Depicts melting pocket watches draped across a barren Catalonian dreamscape beside the cliffs of Port Lligat.

photos.title: The Elephants — Salvador Dalí, 1948
photos.description: Striking 1948 surrealist painting by Salvador Dalí featuring two towering elephants walking on impossibly spindly, multi-jointed arachnid legs while carrying ancient obelisks across a fiery dusk plain.

photos.title: Metamorphosis of Narcissus — Salvador Dalí, 1937
photos.description: Paranoiac-critical masterpiece painted in 1937 by Salvador Dalí (Tate Modern, London), pairing the kneeling figure of Narcissus gazing into a pool with a petrified stone hand holding a cracked bulb from which a narcissus flower blooms.

photos.title: Future Pilots — Aleksandr Deyneka, 1938, State Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow, Russia
photos.description: Iconic Socialist Realist oil painting by Aleksandr Deyneka depicting three sun-drenched Soviet youths sitting on the embankment at Sevastopol, gazing out as a seaplane climbs into the summer sky above the Black Sea.

photos.title: The Traveller — Lyubov Popova, 1915
photos.description: Dynamic 1915 Cubo-Futurist oil painting ('Traveling Woman', Norton Simon Museum) by Russian avant-garde pioneer Lyubov Popova, fragmenting a train passenger, luggage, and passing signage into interlocking planes of motion.

photos.title: Spatial Force Construction — Lyubov Popova, 1921
photos.description: Constructivist oil and marble dust on plywood composition (1920–1921) by Russian avant-garde artist Lyubov Popova, using intersecting diagonal vectors to create dynamic spatial tension.

photos.title: Painterly Architectonic — Lyubov Popova, 1917
photos.description: Suprematist-Constructivist oil painting by Lyubov Popova (National Galleries of Scotland), layering bold geometric wedges of crimson, black, ochre, and white into a balanced architectural rhythm.

photos.title: The Last Supper — Leonardo da Vinci, c. 1495 to 1498
photos.description: The Last Supper (Italian: Il Cenacolo [il tʃeˈnaːkolo] or L'Ultima Cena [ˈlultima ˈtʃeːna]) is a mural painting by the Italian High Renaissance artist Leonardo da Vinci, dated to c. 1495–1498, housed in the refectory of the Convent of Santa Maria delle Grazie in Milan, Italy.

photos.title: Lady with an Ermine — Leonardo da Vinci, c. 1490
photos.description: Exquisite High Renaissance portrait painted around 1489–1490 by Leonardo da Vinci in Milan (Czartoryski Museum, Kraków), portraying Cecilia Gallerani, mistress of Ludovico Sforza, turning gracefully while cradling a white stoat.

photos.title: Fountain — Marcel Duchamp, 1917
photos.description: Fountain was a readymade sculpture attributed to Marcel Duchamp in 1917, consisting of a porcelain urinal signed "R. Mutt".

photos.title: Nude Descending a Staircase No. 2 — Marcel Duchamp, 1912
photos.description: Nude Descending a Staircase, No. 2 (French: Nu descendant un escalier n° 2) is a 1912 painting by Marcel Duchamp.

photos.title: The Bride Stripped Bare by Her Bachelors — Marcel Duchamp, Even
photos.description: The Bride Stripped Bare by Her Bachelors, Even (in French : La mariée mise à nu par ses célibataires, même), also called The Large Glass (in French : Le Grand Verre), is an artwork by Marcel Duchamp over 9 feet (2.7 m) tall and almost 6 feet (1.76m) wide.

photos.title: Portrait of Adele Bloch Bauer I — Gustav Klimt, 1907
photos.description: Opulent 1907 'Woman in Gold' masterpiece by Gustav Klimt at the Neue Galerie, New York. Painted with oil, silver, and gold leaf on canvas, it crowns Klimt's Golden Phase with Byzantine mosaic brilliance.

photos.title: Judith and the Head of Holofernes — Gustav Klimt, 1901
photos.description: Sensual 1901 Vienna Secession oil and gold leaf painting ('Judith I', Belvedere Museum, Vienna) by Gustav Klimt, depicting the biblical heroine holding the severed head of Holofernes beneath a gilded collar of figs and vines.

photos.title: Impression Sunrise — Claude Monet, 1872
photos.description: Seminal 1872 oil painting by Claude Monet (Musée Marmottan Monet, Paris) depicting the mist-shrouded port of Le Havre at daybreak. Its title inspired critic Louis Leroy to coin the name of the Impressionist movement.

photos.title: Water Lilies — Claude Monet, c. 1916
photos.description: Water Lilies (French: Nymphéas [nɛ̃.fe.a]) is a series of approximately 250 oil paintings by French Impressionist Claude Monet (1840–1926). The paintings depict his flower garden at his home in Giverny, and were the main focus of his artistic production during the last 31 years of his life. Many of the works were painted while Monet suffered from cataracts.

photos.title: Woman with a Parasol — Claude Monet, 1875
photos.description: Woman with a Parasol – Madame Monet and Her Son is an oil-on-canvas painting by Claude Monet from 1875. The Impressionist work depicts his wife Camille Monet and their son Jean Monet in the period from 1871 to 1877 while they were living in Argenteuil, capturing a moment on a stroll on a windy summer's day.

photos.title: The Surrender of Breda — Diego Velázquez, 1635
photos.description: La rendición de Breda (English: The Surrender of Breda, also known as Las lanzas – The Lances) is a painting by the Spanish Golden Age painter Diego Velázquez. He painted it during the years 1634 and 1635, inspired by his visit to Italy with Ambrogio Spinola, the Genoese-born Spanish general who conquered Breda on June 5, 1625.

photos.title: Portrait of Pope Innocent X — Diego Velázquez, c. 1650
photos.description: Portrait of Innocent X is a c. 1650 oil on canvas painting by Spanish artist Diego Velázquez, depicting Pope Innocent X, head of the Catholic Church from 1644 to 1655.

photos.title: The Triumphal Procession of Maximilian I — Hans Burgkmair, c. 1512 to 1519
photos.description: Monumental Northern Renaissance woodcut frieze designed by Hans Burgkmair the Elder (1512–1519) for Holy Roman Emperor Maximilian I, depicting an extravagant imperial parade of knights, musicians, and exotic emissaries.

photos.title: Emperor Maximilian I — Hans Burgkmair, 1508
photos.description: Pioneering 1508 chiaroscuro woodcut by Augsburg Renaissance master Hans Burgkmair the Elder (National Gallery of Art, Washington), depicting Holy Roman Emperor Maximilian I in full Gothic plate armor on horseback.

photos.title: The Weisskunig — Hans Burgkmair, c. 1514 to 1516
photos.description: Intricate Renaissance woodcut illustration by Hans Burgkmair the Elder for 'Der Weisskunig' (The White King, c. 1514–1516), the chivalric romance and veiled autobiography of Emperor Maximilian I.

photos.title: The Ancient of Days — William Blake, 1794
photos.description: The Ancient of Days is a design by William Blake, originally published as the frontispiece to the 1794 work Europe a Prophecy. It draws its name from one of God's titles in the Book of Daniel and shows Urizen crouching in a circular design with a cloud-like background.

photos.title: The Great Red Dragon and the Woman Clothed with the Sun — William Blake, c. 1805
photos.description: The Great Red Dragon paintings are a series of watercolour paintings by the English poet and painter William Blake, created between 1805 and 1810. It was during this period that Blake was commissioned to create over one hundred paintings intended to illustrate books of the Bible.

photos.title: Newton — William Blake, 1795
photos.description: Newton is a monotype by the English poet, painter and printmaker William Blake first completed in 1795, but reworked and reprinted in 1805. It is one of the 12 "Large Colour Prints" or "Large Colour Printed Drawings" created between 1795 and 1805, which also include his series of images on the biblical ruler Nebuchadnezzar.

photos.title: Vasco da Gama Before the Zamorin — José María Veloso Salgado, c. 1890s
photos.description: Grand 1898 historical canvas by Luso-Spanish academic master José Maria Veloso Salgado (Sociedade de Geografia de Lisboa), depicting Portuguese explorer Vasco da Gama presenting King Manuel I's letter to the Zamorin of Calicut in 1498.

photos.title: As Ciências Físico-Naturais — José María Veloso Salgado, 1917
photos.description: Allegorical mural 'As Ciências Físico-Naturais' (The Physical and Natural Sciences, 1917) painted by José Maria Veloso Salgado for the Rectorate of the University of Porto.

photos.title: Portrait of Virginie Demont-Breton — José María Veloso Salgado, 1894
photos.description: Refined 1894 salon portrait of French painter Virginie Demont-Breton by José Maria Veloso Salgado, demonstrating his mastery of luminous naturalism and academic portraiture.

photos.title: Procession of the Trolls — Artuš Scheiner, c. 1920s
photos.description: Whimsical Art Nouveau watercolor illustration 'Procession of the Trolls' ('Umzug der Trolle') by Czech artist and illustrator Artuš Scheiner, celebrated for his richly detailed Central European fairy-tale scenes.

photos.title: Amis and Amil — Artuš Scheiner, c. 1920s
photos.description: Romantic medieval chivalric illustration for 'Amis and Amil' by Czech golden-age illustrator Artuš Scheiner, blending crisp Secessionist linework with jewel-toned gouache.

photos.title: The Son of Man — René Magritte, 1964
photos.description: Iconic 1964 surrealist self-portrait by Belgian painter René Magritte, depicting a man in an overcoat and bowler hat standing before a low wall and overcast sea, his face obscured by a hovering green apple.

photos.title: The Treachery of Images — René Magritte, 1929
photos.description: Philosophical 1929 surrealist painting by René Magritte (Los Angeles County Museum of Art), depicting a smoker's pipe above the cursive French inscription 'Ceci n'est pas une pipe' ('This is not a pipe').

photos.title: Golconda — René Magritte, 1953
photos.description: Celebrated 1953 surrealist oil painting by René Magritte (Menil Collection, Houston), portraying dozens of nearly identical men in dark overcoats and bowler hats suspended like raindrops against a bright sky and red-roofed town.

photos.title: The Tree of Life — Ignacio de Ries, 1653
photos.description: Famous 1653 Spanish Baroque allegorical canvas ('El Árbol de la Vida', Segovia Cathedral) by Flemish-born painter Ignacio de Ries. Depicts Christ warning that death cuts down the tree of earthly pleasures while the Devil pulls its trunk.

photos.title: The Baptism of Christ — Ignacio de Ries, 1653
photos.description: Dramatic 1653 Spanish Baroque painting 'The Baptism of Christ' by Ignacio de Ries in Segovia Cathedral, strongly influenced by the tenebrism and rich color of Francisco de Zurbarán.

photos.title: Saints Leander and Isidore — Ignacio de Ries, 17th century
photos.description: Baroque canvas 'Saints Leander and Isidore' by 17th-century Seville master Ignacio de Ries, showcasing sculptural drapery and warm liturgical chiaroscuro.

photos.title: Virgil and Dante Before Cato — Filippo Bigioli, 19th century
photos.description: Romantic Italian historical painting 'Virgil and Dante Before Cato' by 19th-century painter Filippo Bigioli, part of his celebrated cycle illustrating scenes from Dante Alighieri's Divine Comedy.

photos.title: The Third of May 1808 — Francisco Goya, 1814
photos.description: The Third of May 1808 in Madrid (commonly known as The Third of May 1808) and also known, in Spanish, as El tres de mayo de 1808 en Madrid or Los fusilamientos de la montaña del Príncipe Pío, or Los fusilamientos del tres de mayo, is a painting completed in 1814 by the Spanish painter Francisco Goya.

photos.title: Saturn Devouring His Son — Francisco Goya, c. 1820 to 1823
photos.description: Saturn Devouring His Son (Spanish: Saturno devorando a su hijo; also known as Saturn) is a painting by Spanish artist Francisco Goya. The work is one of the 14 so-called Black Paintings that Goya painted directly on the walls of his house some time between 1820 and 1823.

photos.title: The Nude Maja — Francisco Goya, c. 1797 to 1800
photos.description: The Naked Maja or The Nude Maja (Spanish: La maja desnuda [la ˈmaxa ðesˈnuða]) is an oil-on-canvas painting made around 1797–1800 by the Spanish artist Francisco Goya, and has been in the Museo del Prado in Madrid since 1901.

photos.title: The Two Fridas — Frida Kahlo, 1939
photos.description: Monumental 1939 double self-portrait by Mexican artist Frida Kahlo (Museo de Arte Moderno, Mexico City), portraying two seated versions of herself—one in European Victorian lace and one in traditional Tehuana dress—linked by exposed hearts and arteries.

photos.title: Self Portrait with Thorn Necklace and Hummingbird — Frida Kahlo, 1940
photos.description: Intense 1940 oil self-portrait by Frida Kahlo (Harry Ransom Center, Austin), depicting the artist framed by lush tropical foliage with a spider monkey, a black cat, and a bleeding necklace of thorns from which a dead hummingbird hangs.

photos.title: The Broken Column — Frida Kahlo, 1944
photos.description: Piercing 1944 oil on masonite self-portrait by Frida Kahlo (Museo Dolores Olmedo, Mexico City), painted after spinal surgery. Shows her torso split open to reveal a cracked Ionic column in place of her spine, bound in a steel orthopedic brace.

photos.title: The Last Judgment — Michelangelo, 1536 to 1541
photos.description: The Last Judgment (Italian: Il Giudizio Universale) is a fresco by the Italian Renaissance painter Michelangelo covering the whole altar wall of the Sistine Chapel in Vatican City. It is a depiction of the Second Coming of Christ and the final and eternal judgment by God of all humanity.

photos.title: The Delphic Sibyl — Michelangelo, 1508 to 1512
photos.description: The Delphic Sibyl was a prophetess associated with early religious practices in Ancient Greece and is said to have been venerated from before the Trojan Wars as an important oracle. At that time Delphi was a place of worship for Gaia, the mother goddess connected with fertility rituals that are thought to have existed throughout the ancient Mediterranean world.

photos.title: The Hunters in the Snow — Pieter Bruegel the Elder, 1565
photos.description: The Hunters in the Snow (Dutch: Jagers in de Sneeuw), also known as The Return of the Hunters, is a 1565 oil-on-wood painting by Pieter Bruegel the Elder. The Northern Renaissance work is one of a series of works, five of which still survive, that depict different times of the year.

photos.title: The Tower of Babel — Pieter Bruegel the Elder, 1563
photos.description: Monumental 1563 Northern Renaissance oil on oak panel by Pieter Bruegel the Elder (Kunsthistorisches Museum, Vienna), modeling the biblical Tower of Babel after the Roman Colosseum with extraordinary architectural and human detail.

photos.title: The Peasant Wedding — Pieter Bruegel the Elder, c. 1567
photos.description: The Peasant Wedding is a 1567 genre painting by the Dutch and Flemish Renaissance painter and printmaker Pieter Bruegel the Elder, one of his many depicting peasant life. It is now in the Kunsthistorisches Museum, Vienna.

photos.title: An Experiment on a Bird in the Air Pump — Joseph Wright of Derby, 1768
photos.description: An Experiment on a Bird in the Air Pump is a 1768 oil-on-canvas painting by Joseph Wright of Derby, one of a number of candlelit scenes that Wright painted during the 1760s. The painting departed from convention of the time by depicting a scientific subject in the reverential manner formerly reserved for scenes of historical or religious significance.

photos.title: A Philosopher Lecturing on the Orrery — Joseph Wright of Derby, c. 1766
photos.description: A Philosopher Lecturing on the Orrery, or the full title, A Philosopher giving that Lecture on the Orrery in which a lamp is put in place of the Sun, is a 1766 painting by Joseph Wright of Derby depicting a lecturer giving a demonstration of an orrery – a mechanical model of the Solar System – to a small audience.

photos.title: The Alchemist Discovering Phosphorus — Joseph Wright of Derby, 1771
photos.description: The Alchemist Discovering Phosphorus is a painting by Joseph Wright of Derby originally completed in 1771 then reworked in 1795. The full title of the painting is The Alchymist, in Search of the Philosopher's Stone, Discovers Phosphorus, and prays for the successful Conclusion of his operation, as was the custom of the Ancient Chymical Astrologers.

photos.title: The Apotheosis of War — Vasily Vereshchagin, 1871
photos.description: The Apotheosis of War (Russian: Апофеоз войны) is an 1871 painting by Russian war artist Vasily Vereshchagin. Following his completion of the painting, Vereshchagin dedicated his work "to all great conquerors, past, present and to come".

photos.title: The Death of General Skobelev — Vasily Vereshchagin, 1880
photos.description: Sweeping 19th-century realist war canvas ('Skobelev at Shipka') by Russian painter Vasily Vereshchagin, depicting General Mikhail Skobelev riding past cheering Russian regiments across the snow-covered Shipka Pass battlefield alongside its dead.

photos.title: The Doors of Tamerlane — Vasily Vereshchagin, 1872
photos.description: Masterpiece of Russian Orientalist realism painted in 1872 by Vasily Vereshchagin (Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow), depicting two heavily armed Central Asian guards standing watch before the intricately carved palace doors of Timur (Tamerlane) in Samarkand.

photos.title: The Arnolfini Portrait — Jan van Eyck, 1434
photos.description: Groundbreaking 1434 Early Netherlandish oil on oak panel by Jan van Eyck (National Gallery, London), portraying Italian merchant Giovanni di Nicolao Arnolfini and his wife in Bruges with a famously detailed convex mirror and brass chandelier.

photos.title: The Ghent Altarpiece — Jan van Eyck, 1432
photos.description: The Ghent Altarpiece, also called the Adoration of the Mystic Lamb (Dutch: De aanbidding van het Lam Gods), is a very large and complex 15th-century polyptych altarpiece in St Bavo's Cathedral, Ghent, Belgium. It was begun around the mid-1420s and completed by 1432, and it is attributed to the Early Netherlandish painters and brothers Hubert and Jan van Eyck.

photos.title: The Madonna of Chancellor Rolin — Jan van Eyck, c. 1435
photos.description: Luminous c. 1435 Early Netherlandish oil panel by Jan van Eyck (Musée du Louvre, Paris), depicting Nicolas Rolin, Chancellor of Burgundy, kneeling in prayer before the Virgin Mary and Infant Christ overlooking a panoramic river city.

photos.title: Madonna — Edvard Munch, 1894 to 1895
photos.description: Madonna is the usual title given to several versions of a composition by the Norwegian expressionist painter Edvard Munch showing a bare-breasted half-length female figure created between 1892 and 1895 using oil paint on canvas.

photos.title: The Dance of Life — Edvard Munch, 1899 to 1900
photos.description: The Dance of Life or Life's Dance is an 1899–1900 expressionist painting by Edvard Munch, now in the National Museum of Norway, in Oslo. Olaf Schou purchased the painting in Oslo in 1910, immediately presenting it to the National Gallery.

photos.title: The Garden of Earthly Delights — Hieronymus Bosch, c. 1490 to 1510
photos.description: Enigmatic Early Netherlandish oak triptych painted between 1490 and 1510 by Hieronymus Bosch (Museo del Prado, Madrid), tracing humanity from the Garden of Eden through a teeming panorama of earthly temptations to a surreal musical Hell.

photos.title: The Temptation of St Anthony — Hieronymus Bosch, c. 1500
photos.description: The Temptation of St. Anthony is a painting of disputed authorship, attributed to either the Early Netherlandish artist Hieronymus Bosch or a follower. It is now in the Museo del Prado, in Madrid.

photos.title: The Haywain — Hieronymus Bosch, c. 1510 to 1516
photos.description: Satirical c. 1516 triptych by Hieronymus Bosch (Museo del Prado, Madrid), illustrating the Flemish proverb that the world is a haystack from which everyone plucks as much as they can, oblivious to Christ above and Hell ahead.

photos.title: Guernica — Pablo Picasso, 1937
photos.description: Monumental 1937 anti-war oil painting by Pablo Picasso (Museo Reina Sofía, Madrid), created in stark grisaille black, white, and grey in response to the bombing of the Basque town of Guernica during the Spanish Civil War.

photos.title: Les Demoiselles d'Avignon — Pablo Picasso, 1907
photos.description: Les Demoiselles d'Avignon (pronounced [le demwazɛl d‿aviɲɔ̃]; The Young Ladies of Avignon, originally titled The Brothel of Avignon) is a large oil painting created in 1907 by the Spanish artist Pablo Picasso. Part of the permanent collection of the Museum of Modern Art in New York, it portrays five nude female prostitutes in a brothel on Carrer d'Avinyó, a street in Barcelona, Spain.

photos.title: The Weeping Woman — Pablo Picasso, 1937
photos.description: Searing 1937 Cubist oil canvas by Pablo Picasso (Tate Modern, London), painted as a coda to 'Guernica' and modeled on Dora Maar, fracturing a grief-stricken face clutching a handkerchief into jagged shards of acid green, yellow, and violet.

photos.title: The Old Fisherman — Tivadar Csontváry Kosztka, 1902
photos.description: Haunting 1902 visionary portrait by Hungarian painter Tivadar Csontváry Kosztka (Ottó Herman Museum, Miskolc). Famous for its bilaterally asymmetric face: mirroring one side reveals a pious man praying above a calm sea, while the other reveals the Devil before a stormy volcano.

photos.title: The Lonely Cedar — Tivadar Csontváry Kosztka, 1907
photos.description: Mystical 1907 post-impressionist canvas by Hungarian visionary Tivadar Csontváry Kosztka ( Janus Pannonius Museum, Pécs), portraying an ancient, wind-sculpted cedar of Lebanon standing sentinel atop a radiant mountain ridge.

photos.title: The Pilgrimage to the Cedars of Lebanon — Tivadar Csontváry Kosztka, 1907
photos.description: Symbolic 1907 masterpiece by Tivadar Csontváry Kosztka (Hungarian National Gallery, Budapest), depicting riders and dancers gathered in ritual celebration around a monumental twin-trunked cedar tree under glowing evening skies.

photos.title: Primavera — Sandro Botticelli, c. 1480
photos.description: Celebrated c. 1480 Italian Renaissance tempera panel by Sandro Botticelli (Uffizi Gallery, Florence), bringing together Venus, Cupid, the Three Graces, Mercury, Flora, and Zephyrus in a lush orange grove carpeted with over 500 identified plant species.

photos.title: The Map of Hell / Chart of Hell — Sandro Botticelli, c. 1480s to 1490s
photos.description: Intricate late-15th-century silverpoint and tempera parchment illumination by Sandro Botticelli (Vatican Library), mapping the nine concentric funnel-shaped circles of Dante's Inferno in breathtaking microscopic detail.

photos.title: The Obliteration Room — Yayoi Kusama, 2002
photos.description: Immersive contemporary installation ('The Obliteration Room') by Japanese avant-garde artist Yayoi Kusama, transforming an entire domestic interior with thousands of vibrant chromatic polka dots.

photos.title: Pumpkin — Yayoi Kusama, 1994
photos.description: Iconic polka-dotted pumpkin sculpture by Japanese contemporary artist Yayoi Kusama, turning the organic gourd form into a hypnotic, rhythmic monument of black-and-yellow dots.

photos.title: Thunderstorm Beneath the Summit — Katsushika Hokusai, c. 1830 to 1832
photos.description: Thunderstorm Beneath the Summit (Japanese: 山下白雨, Hepburn: Sanka hakuu), also known as Rainstorm Beneath the Summit, or sometimes Black Fuji (黒富士 Kurofuji) is a woodcut print by the Japanese ukiyo-e master Hokusai (1760–1849). It is one of the most famous prints from his celebrated Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji series, published c. 1830–1832.

photos.title: Self-Portrait (Autoportrait) — Gerard Sekoto, c. 1947
photos.description: Expressive oil self-portrait by pioneering South African modernist Gerard Sekoto, whose warm, empathetic depictions of township life and human dignity laid the foundation for modern Black South African art.

photos.title: Dar-es-Salaam — J. H. Pierneef, 1926
photos.description: Atmospheric 1926 East African coastal painting 'Dar-es-Salaam' by South African landscape master J. H. Pierneef, blending decorative post-impressionist line with warm tropical light.

photos.title: Landscape with Clouds — J. H. Pierneef, 1926
photos.description: Majestic 1926 painting 'Landscape with Clouds' by J. H. Pierneef, featuring his signature towering cumulus cloud formations rising over vast Southern African plains.

photos.title: Arab — Irma Stern, 1939, Irma Stern Museum, Cape Town, South Africa
photos.description: Celebrated 1945 oil portrait ('Arabier') by South African expressionist Irma Stern, inspired by her voyages to Zanzibar and painted with rich, jewel-like Fauvist color and dignified characterization.

photos.title: Bust of Nefertiti — Thutmose, c. 1345 BC, Neues Museum, Berlin, Germany
photos.description: Painted stucco-coated limestone portrait bust of Great Royal Wife Nefertiti of Eighteenth-Dynasty Egypt, sculpted by the royal master Thutmose at Amarna and celebrated for its symmetrical elegance.

photos.title: Pietà — Michelangelo, 1499, St. Peter's Basilica, Vatican City
photos.description: High Renaissance Carrara marble masterpiece carved by a 24-year-old Michelangelo Buonarroti, depicting the Virgin Mary cradling the body of Jesus with serene classical grace and virtuosic drapery.

photos.title: Laocoön and His Sons — Agesander, Athenodoros & Polydoros of Rhodes, c. 40 BC, Vatican Museums, Vatican City
photos.description: Monumental Hellenistic marble group unearthed in Rome in 1506, capturing the Trojan priest Laocoön and his two sons writhing in agony as giant sea serpents coil around them.

photos.title: Apollo and Daphne — Gian Lorenzo Bernini, 1625, Galleria Borghese, Rome, Italy
photos.description: Baroque life-size Carrara marble sculpture by Gian Lorenzo Bernini capturing the dramatic Ovidian metamorphosis at the exact instant laurel bark and leaves envelop the fleeing nymph Daphne.

photos.title: Ecstasy of Saint Teresa — Gian Lorenzo Bernini, 1652, Santa Maria della Vittoria, Rome, Italy
photos.description: High Baroque sculptural altarpiece in the Cornaro Chapel by Gian Lorenzo Bernini, depicting the Spanish mystic Teresa of Ávila floating on marble clouds illuminated by gilded bronze rays.

photos.title: Discobolus (Discus Thrower) — Myron (Lancellotti Roman Marble), c. 450 BC, Palazzo Massimo, Rome, Italy
photos.description: Classical Greek athletic ideal originally cast in bronze by Myron of Eleutherae and preserved in the Lancellotti Roman marble copy, poised at the coiled apex of a discus throw.

photos.title: Statue of Liberty (Liberty Enlightening the World) — Frédéric Auguste Bartholdi, 1886, New York Harbor, USA
photos.description: Colossal neoclassical copper monument designed by Frédéric Auguste Bartholdi with an internal iron framework by Gustave Eiffel, gifted by France to the United States on Liberty Island.

photos.title: Perseus with the Head of Medusa — Benvenuto Cellini, 1554, Loggia dei Lanzi, Florence, Italy
photos.description: Mannerist bronze tour de force cast by Benvenuto Cellini for Duke Cosimo I de' Medici, showing the mythological hero standing triumphantly over Medusa's body and raising her severed head.

photos.title: The Kiss (Le Baiser) — Auguste Rodin, 1889, Musée Rodin, Paris, France
photos.description: Sensuous white marble sculpture by Auguste Rodin depicting the medieval Italian lovers Paolo and Francesca from Dante's Inferno locked in a timeless embrace emerging from rough-hewn stone.

photos.title: Dying Gaul (Capitoline Gaul) — Ancient Roman Marble after Hellenistic Bronze, c. 220 BC, Capitoline Museums, Rome, Italy
photos.description: Poignant ancient Roman marble copy of a lost Pergamene bronze commemorating King Attalus I's victory over the Galatians, celebrated for its noble pathos and anatomical realism.

photos.title: Farnese Hercules — Glykon of Athens after Lysippos, c. 216 AD, National Archaeological Museum, Naples, Italy
photos.description: Monumental Roman marble statue recovered from the Baths of Caracalla, depicting a weary, heavily muscled Hercules leaning on his club draped with the Nemean lion's pelt.

photos.title: Charioteer of Delphi (Heniokhos) — Ancient Greek Bronze, c. 474 BC, Delphi Archaeological Museum, Greece
photos.description: Rare surviving life-size Early Classical Greek bronze cast to commemorate Polyzalos of Gela's victory at the Pythian Games, preserving inlaid glass eyes and copper eyelashes.

photos.title: Artemision Bronze (Zeus or Poseidon) — Classical Greek Bronze, c. 460 BC, National Archaeological Museum, Athens, Greece
photos.description: Over-life-size Classical Greek original bronze recovered from an ancient shipwreck off Cape Artemision, capturing the god of sky or sea poised to hurl a thunderbolt or trident.

photos.title: Mask of Agamemnon — Mycenaean Gold Funerary Mask, c. 1550 BC, National Archaeological Museum, Athens, Greece
photos.description: Beaten sheet-gold royal death mask excavated by Heinrich Schliemann from Shaft Grave V at Mycenae in 1876, an emblem of Bronze Age Aegean kingship.

photos.title: The Seated Scribe — Old Kingdom Painted Limestone, c. 2500 BC, Saqqara / Musée du Louvre, Paris, France
photos.description: Fourth- or Fifth-Dynasty painted limestone statue from Saqqara with lifelike rock-crystal, magnesite, and copper-inlaid eyes, portraying an alert Egyptian official with papyrus scroll in hand.

photos.title: Colossal Olmec Head (San Lorenzo Monument 1) — Olmec Civilization, c. 1200 BC, Xalapa Museum of Anthropology, Veracruz, Mexico
photos.description: Multi-ton basalt boulder carved by Mesoamerica's mother culture into a commanding ruler portrait wearing a close-fitting helmet, transported miles from the Tuxtla Mountains.

photos.title: Leshan Giant Buddha — Tang Dynasty Cliff Sculpture, 803 AD, Leshan, Sichuan, China
photos.description: Standing 71 meters tall at the confluence of the Min, Qingyi, and Dadu rivers, this red sandstone Maitreya Buddha carved during the Tang Dynasty is the largest pre-modern stone sculpture on Earth.

photos.title: Great Buddha of Kamakura (Kamakura Daibutsu) — Kamakura Period Bronze, c. 1252, Kōtoku-in, Kamakura, Japan
photos.description: Monumental outdoor bronze statue of Amida Buddha cast in the 13th century at Kōtoku-in temple, surviving a 1498 tsunami that swept away its original wooden hall.

photos.title: Augustus of Prima Porta — Imperial Roman Marble, c. 20 BC, Vatican Museums, Vatican City
photos.description: Full-length marble portrait of Rome's first emperor Augustus in ceremonial cuirass carved with cosmic and Parthian victory reliefs, discovered at Empress Livia's villa at Prima Porta.

photos.title: Winged Bull (Lamassu) from Citadel of Sargon II — Neo-Assyrian Limestone, c. 710 BC, Dur-Sharrukin / Louvre, Paris, France
photos.description: Colossal monolithic gypsum-alabaster guardian deity with a bearded human head, eagle wings, and five bull legs sculpted to appear stationary from the front and striding from the side.

photos.title: Hagia Sophia — Anthemius of Tralles & Isidore of Miletus, 537 AD, Istanbul, Turkey
photos.description: Revolutionary Byzantine cathedral commissioned by Emperor Justinian I, crowned by a pendentive dome that seemed 'suspended from heaven by a golden chain' and later flanked by Ottoman minarets.

photos.title: Al-Khazneh (The Treasury) — Nabataean Kingdom, c. 1st c. AD, Petra, Jordan
photos.description: Elaborate Hellenistic-style royal mausoleum carved directly into a rose-red sandstone cliff face at the mouth of the Siq gorge by the Nabataean caravan empire.

photos.title: Court of the Lions, Alhambra Palace — Nasrid Dynasty, 1380, Granada, Spain
photos.description: Jewel of Moorish palace architecture in Andalusia, uniting a central alabaster fountain borne by twelve marble lions with filigree stucco arches and muqarnas vaults.

photos.title: Basílica de la Sagrada Família — Antoni Gaudí, begun 1882, Barcelona, Spain
photos.description: Antoni Gaudí's visionary Catalan Modernisme basilica, fusing Gothic structural geometry with organic hyperboloid vaults and towering sculptural facades.

photos.title: The Pantheon — Roman Empire under Hadrian, c. 126 AD, Rome, Italy
photos.description: Best-preserved monument of ancient Rome, combining a Corinthian granite portico with the world's largest unreinforced concrete dome pierced by a 9-meter central oculus.

photos.title: Saint Basil's Cathedral — Postnik Yakovlev, 1561, Red Square, Moscow, Russia
photos.description: Cathedral of Vasily the Blessed commissioned by Ivan the Terrible on Red Square, famous for its nine flame-like polychrome onion domes rising above the Moscow River.

photos.title: Neuschwanstein Castle — King Ludwig II of Bavaria, 1886, Hohenschwangau, Bavaria, Germany
photos.description: Nineteenth-century Romanesque Revival cliffside palace built by King Ludwig II in the Bavarian Alps as a poetic homage to Richard Wagner's operas.

photos.title: Mont-Saint-Michel Abbey — Medieval Norman Architecture, 11th–16th c., Normandy, France
photos.description: Fortified Benedictine abbey crowning a tidal granite island off the coast of Normandy, ascending in tiers from medieval ramparts to a soaring Gothic spire.

photos.title: Potala Palace — 5th Dalai Lama, 1649, Lhasa, Tibet, China
photos.description: Thirteen-story dzong fortress rising 117 meters atop Marpo Ri hill in the Lhasa Valley, comprising over a thousand rooms inside the monumental White and Red Palaces.

photos.title: Temple of Heaven (Hall of Prayer for Good Harvests) — Ming Dynasty, 1420, Beijing, China
photos.description: Triple-gabled circular imperial wooden hall resting on a three-tiered white marble terrace, built entirely without nails where Ming and Qing emperors prayed for abundant harvests.

photos.title: Himeji Castle (Shirasagi-jō) — Ikeda Terumasa, 1609, Himeji, Hyōgo, Japan
photos.description: Japan's premier surviving feudal hilltop castle complex, nicknamed the White Egret Castle for its brilliant white plastered earthen walls and multi-layered winged roofs.

photos.title: Kinkaku-ji (Temple of the Golden Pavilion) — Ashikaga Yoshimitsu, 1397, Kyoto, Japan
photos.description: Muromachi-period Zen Buddhist pavilion in northern Kyoto whose top two stories are clad in pure gold leaf, mirrored in the tranquil waters of Kyōko-chi (Mirror Pond).

photos.title: Meenakshi Amman Temple — Nayak Dynasty, 16th c., Madurai, Tamil Nadu, India
photos.description: Dravidian temple complex on the Vaigai River famed for its fourteen towering gopuram gateway towers encrusted with tens of thousands of vividly painted stucco deities.

photos.title: Hawa Mahal (Palace of Winds) — Maharaja Sawai Pratap Singh, 1799, Jaipur, Rajasthan, India
photos.description: Five-story red and pink sandstone honeycomb facade built by architect Lal Chand Ustad with 953 carved jharokha lattice windows that channel cooling breezes.

photos.title: Shah Mosque (Imam Mosque) — Safavid Empire under Abbas the Great, 1629, Isfahan, Iran
photos.description: Masterpiece of Persian Safavid architecture on Naqsh-e Jahan Square, clad in seven-color mosaic tilework and crowned by a double-shelled turquoise dome.

photos.title: Dome of the Rock — Umayyad Caliphate under Abd al-Malik, 691 AD, Jerusalem
photos.description: Octagonal Early Islamic shrine on the Temple Mount, the world's oldest surviving work of Islamic architecture, crowned by a gleaming gilded dome above Ottoman Iznik tiles.

photos.title: Great Temple of Abu Simbel — Pharaoh Ramesses II, c. 1264 BC, Nubia / Aswan, Egypt
photos.description: Monumental rock-cut Nubian temple guarded by four 20-meter seated colossi of Ramesses II, relocated block by block in 1968 to save it from the rising waters of Lake Nasser.

photos.title: Sydney Opera House — Jørn Utzon, 1973, Sydney, New South Wales, Australia
photos.description: Twentieth-century expressionist architectural icon on Bennelong Point, composed of interlocking precast concrete shells clad in over one million Swedish ceramic tiles.

photos.title: Florence Cathedral (Santa Maria del Fiore) — Filippo Brunelleschi, 1436, Florence, Italy
photos.description: Cradle of Renaissance engineering crowned by Filippo Brunelleschi's self-supporting herringbone brick double dome, the largest masonry vault ever constructed.

photos.title: Registan Square Madrasas (Ulugh Beg, Sher-Dor & Tilya-Kori) — Timurid & Shaybanid Dynasties, 15th–17th c., Samarkand, Uzbekistan
photos.description: Monumental ensemble of three grand Islamic madrasas framing the heart of ancient Samarkand along the Silk Road, adorned with azure ribbed domes and glazed majolica.
